why: The predicate has three arms — a `?` label, an [open] claim in the body, and an open tag in a property the class declared `type: claim` — and `corpus/` carries one node flagged by each, never two ways. A server implementing two of them returns two nodes instead of three, and which two names the arm it is missing: no `concept/traversal` is the label arm, no `concept/retrieval` the text arm, no `concept/embedding-space` the declared-field arm. The third is the one that goes unnoticed, because a corpus that declares no `type: claim` property makes it match nothing and a two-arm server answers identically everywhere.
